judgements.referenceQuote: 12th Managing Director of the International Monetary FundIncumbentAssumed office 1 October 2019
judgements.evidenceQuote: She became Managing Director of the IMF on October 1, 2019.
judgements.rationale: The dossier states the role and the exact start date (1 October 2019), and a separate claim notes she is the first person from an emerging economy to head the IMF, but no dossier statement gives the ordinal '12th Managing Director', so the reference fact is only partly covered.

judgements.referenceQuote: Chief Executive of the World Bank GroupIn office2 January 2017 – 1 October 2019
judgements.evidenceQuote: She was CEO of IBRD and IDA from 2017-2019, and interim President from February 2019.
judgements.rationale: The dossier covers the CEO role (2017-2019) and the interim presidency from February 2019 (another claim says 'for three months', consistent with Feb–Apr 2019), but omits the precise start/end dates (2 Jan 2017, 1 Oct 2019, 8 Apr 2019) and the detail that the CEO post was established for her and abolished afterwards.

judgements.referenceQuote: European Commissioner for Budget and Human ResourcesIn office1 November 2014 – 31 December 2016
judgements.evidenceQuote: her role as European Commission Vice President for Budget and Human Resources (2014-2016)
judgements.rationale: The dossier states the Budget and Human Resources portfolio for 2014-2016, but renders the title as 'Vice President' rather than 'European Commissioner', gives only years rather than 1 Nov 2014–31 Dec 2016, and says nothing about managing the EU's budget and staff through the aftermath of the Eurozone debt crisis.

usefulness.rationale: Understanding is strong: the dossier traces a complete arc — born Sofia 1953, World Bank environmental economist from 1993, VP/Corporate Secretary 2008, EU Commissioner for Humanitarian Aid (2010-2014) and Commission VP for Budget (2014-2016), World Bank CEO 2017-2019, IMF Managing Director since 1 October 2019, reappointed for a second term in 2024 — plus substantive work content (COVID $1T mobilization, SDR positions, Argentina engagement, Ukraine, AI-and-jobs warnings), ideas, awards, and the Doing Business ethics probe. A reader clearly learns who she is and what she did. RemainingQuestions is weak: the dossier never states what it does not know; uncertainty is only implicit in contested/claimed status labels, and several entries are bare 'statement' placeholders with generic quotes that leave obvious gaps (family, education verification, current priorities) unacknowledged. ConversationReadiness is decent — current role, second term, recent 2026 connections (Milei, Caputo, Tenreyro appointment) and policy positions are meeting-ready — but held to 2 by internal contradictions (a 2019 'first trip to Argentina as IMF chief' vs. 2026 trips described the same way, stale 'scheduled to visit' items) and placeholder claims that could mislead preparation.
